raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it. That is the system I know best, and after 35 years I would not complicate it. Because some people in my household work off-farm, I will keep management steady and practical rather than risky. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect wheat at key stages and give maize one or two timely waterings if rain is short. For seed, I will use better-performing seed rather than traditional saved seed, because on a small area I care more about stable yield than saving a little on seed cost. I will put more fertilizer into wheat and maize than a very low-input farmer would, but not excessively, because I want dependable grain and I know my land has to support two crops in one year. I will use rotary tillage because it fits a small farm like mine, handles the straw and stubble reasonably well, and is simpler for me to manage. I will still spray for the main diseases, insects, and weeds, but I will keep the number of applications limited to what I think is necessary. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield. I will aim for a stable, workable year with solid wheat and maize production from the same 5 mu.
